The rain didn’t fall; it hammered. It struck the glass of the lantern room with the rhythmic violence of a thousand tiny fists, blurring the horizon into a smear of charcoal and slate. Elias wiped the condensation from the lens, his breath fogging the cold air, when the radio crackled.

It wasn’t the static of the storm. It was a voice, clear as a bell, cutting through the white noise.

"Stop the rotation, Elias. Now."

Elias froze, his hand hovering over the heavy iron wheel. He looked at the radio, then at the dark, churning sea. "Who is this? This is a restricted frequency."

"You’re not listening," the voice said. It was his own voice, but older, raspy, stripped of the youthful vigor he still possessed. "The ship. The *Aethelgard*. It’s not coming from the east. It’s coming from the north. If you keep the light rotating, you’ll blind the pilot. He’ll miss the reef. He’ll hit the rocks."
